meta.title: Market Research
meta.subtitle: Critical assessment of the existing BizMatch market-research and interview material
meta.privacy_note: This public report contains aggregate findings only. Participant names, contact details, recordings, transcripts, and other identifying information are intentionally excluded.

executive_conclusion.summary: The existing material is useful exploratory research, but it does not constitute market validation for BizMatch.
findings: Finding a co-founder was not the primary pain identified by the current interview sample.
The correct current recommendation is Narrow the research.
The research does not yet justify Proceed, Pivot, or Stop for the full venture.

research_inventory.clarification: The folder previously described as a “market survey” contains secondary market research. No quantitative survey was found.

rows.material: No distributed survey or response dataset found
Interview tree, prepared guide and KPI document

rows.status: 11 complete, 3 partial, 1 still marked in progress

rows.material: One separate recording without structured transcription

rows.status: Opinions and decisions, not research evidence

useful: The research distinguishes between evidence, estimates, and information gaps.
It acknowledges missing Israeli data about active co-founder searches and willingness to pay.
It identifies liquidity, community-selection bias, and the difference between a match, a meeting, and a partnership.
limitations: International platform activity does not validate urgent Israeli demand.
The TEA population is too broad to serve as BizMatch’s practical TAM.
The estimated SAM of 6,000–12,000 is based on weak proxy assumptions.
Employees are not a valid proxy for co-founder demand.
Business openings and business births are different measurements.
Conflicting GEM figures must not be used without identifying the correct source and year.
The previous 72/100 score creates false precision and must not be used as evidence supporting an MVP.
secondary_research_assessment.scenario_note: Any TAM, SAM, or SOM values in the existing material are scenarios, not validated forecasts.

assessment: Only 2 of the 15 participants were actively looking for a partner.
Seven were already in Customers, Revenue, or Scale.
The sample did not match the intended Validation/MVP ICP.
Recruitment-source data was not consistently preserved.
Convenience-sample and personal-network bias are plausible.
The interviews cannot be treated as representative of Israeli founders.

methodology_problems: BizMatch was introduced before the participant’s problem was independently discovered.
The interview primed participants to discuss partners, trust, and disclosure.
Some raw questions directly introduced AI, swipe, NDA, and matching concepts.
The KPI combined partner, investor, and trust problems even though they are different Jobs to Be Done.
One record intentionally marked a participant as having a partner in order to continue through the interview flow.
“Partner” was not consistently defined as co-founder, ownership partner, business partner, or collaborator.
Personally identifying information was stored alongside research data without a documented anonymization and retention process.

primary_pain.label: identified finding a co-founder as the single problem they would remove
details: More common problems included sales, distribution, cash flow, funding, customers, product-market fit, and operational pressure.
This is an important negative finding, but it does not disprove the problem among a narrower sample of active co-founder seekers.

partner_origin.excluded_record_note: One intentionally invalid record is excluded from the partner-origin analysis.

channels.channel: Studies, programs, or another existing relationship

partner_origin.conclusion: The current alternative is not merely LinkedIn or WhatsApp. It is prior relationships, shared work, and warm introductions.

trust.hypothesis: A structured trial project or collaboration period may create more value than profile matching alone.

conclusions: Selective disclosure is supported as a concern.
The severity and behavioural effect of that concern were not measured.
NDA was not validated as the preferred solution.
NDA friction and abandonment were not tested.

hypothesis_register.hypothesis: Israeli founders struggle to find co-founders
hypothesis_register.detail: Only two active seekers were interviewed

hypothesis_register.hypothesis: The problem is urgent and recurring
hypothesis_register.detail: Not supported by the broad sample

hypothesis_register.hypothesis: Users will provide sufficient profile data
A structured post-match process is needed
Investors want deal flow from a new platform
Sufficient marketplace liquidity can be created in Israel

keep: Raw recordings, JSON, and summaries in the private research repository.
Behaviour-based questions about previous cases, time, money, trust, and partner origin.
Observations about reference checks, shared work, and selective disclosure.
recode: Co-founder versus other types of partners.
Partner, investor, sales, and trust problems.
exclude: Urgency percentages that mix different problems.
Willingness-to-pay assumptions based on money spent solving other problems.

decision_gate.learned: Trust and selective disclosure matter, but partnerships were mainly created through existing relationships and shared experience. Co-founder search was not the primary pain in this sample.
decision_gate.unknown: Urgency among active co-founder seekers, dissatisfaction with alternatives, willingness to switch, NDA value and friction, investor demand, willingness to pay, and marketplace liquidity.
decision_gate.falsification: A focused sample of active Validation/MVP founders may show that the problem is not urgent, warm introductions are sufficient, or users will not complete profiles and participate in curated introductions.
decision_gate.not_allowed: Claim that the need is validated, NDA is the differentiator, willingness to pay exists, the SAM is 6,000–12,000, or a broad MVP should be built.
